contradictions.field: SWE-bench Verified current frontier-model leader and score

candidates.claim: Reports % Resolved out of 500 Verified instances but does not itself assert a single global 'leader' figure that was captured verbatim in this pass

contradictions.delta: Roughly 14+ percentage points between secondary aggregator claims for 'the leader', reflecting different snapshot dates and possibly different task-count/scaffold conditions rather than a true methodology conflict
contradictions.winner: swebench.com is the authoritative single source of truth for SWE-bench Verified scores; secondary aggregator disagreement reflects publication-date drift in a fast-moving field, not a genuine data conflict -- AICoderMap should always cite swebench.com directly, never a secondary aggregator's restated number, for this benchmark

contradictions.field: Bradley-Terry vs. plain Elo superiority under sparse comparison data

candidates.claim: Bradley-Terry MLE is presented as the superior successor to classic Elo for leaderboard ranking generally
'in very sparse regimes (few matches per player), vanilla scalar Elo exhibits lower regret and outperforms richer models (Elo2k, fully pairwise), despite model misspecification'

contradictions.delta: Directionally opposite recommendations depending on data density
contradictions.winner: context-dependent, not a true contradiction: both are correct in their respective regimes -- Bradley-Terry needs enough comparisons per item to estimate reliably, and simple Elo is more robust exactly when data is thin. Practical implication for AICoderMap: if a preset/weighting scheme ever needs pairwise comparative ranking with few observations per model (e.g., a newly-added model), prefer simpler shrinkage/Elo-style estimators over a full Bradley-Terry fit until enough data accrues
